evals.prompt: Audit the dependencies in this project for vulnerabilities
evals.description: Node.js project with a package-lock.json present and npm available. npm audit should be invoked and its output parsed. The report must show the severity breakdown and list at least one advisory.
evals.expected_output: Report identifies the Node.js ecosystem, notes that npm audit was used, and lists lodash 4.17.4 as vulnerable (prototype pollution advisories exist for versions below 4.17.21). Report includes severity, advisory ID, and a recommended fix version.

assertions.text: The report states that npm audit was used to scan dependencies
lodash is listed as a vulnerable package
The report includes a severity level (critical, high, moderate, or low) for the lodash finding
The report recommends a fix or upgrade path for the vulnerable package
No project files were modified — package.json and package-lock.json are unchanged

evals.prompt: Check this Python project for dependency vulnerabilities
evals.description: Python project with a requirements.txt listing a package with a known CVE. pip-audit should be invoked if available; otherwise pip list --outdated is used as a fallback. The report must clearly distinguish between the tool path and the fallback path.
evals.setup:
mkdir -p /tmp/eval-depaudit-1 && cd /tmp/eval-depaudit-1 && git init && cat > requirements.txt << 'EOF'
requests==2.18.0
EOF
evals.expected_output: Report identifies the Python ecosystem, states whether pip-audit was used or a fallback was applied, and flags requests 2.18.0 as outdated or vulnerable. If pip-audit is unavailable, the report explicitly states this and lists packages for manual review.

assertions.text: The report identifies Python as one of the scanned ecosystems
requests 2.18.0 appears in the report (as vulnerable, outdated, or requiring manual review)
The report states which tool was used (pip-audit, safety) or explicitly notes the fallback path if no tool was found
requirements.txt is not modified

evals.description: Monorepo with both a Node.js package.json and a Python requirements.txt at different paths. Both ecosystems must be scanned — the skill must not stop after finding the first manifest.
evals.expected_output: Report covers both the Node.js frontend and the Python backend. Summary table shows findings for both ecosystems. Fallback paths are documented if dedicated tools are absent.

assertions.text: The report mentions Node.js or npm as a scanned ecosystem
The report mentions Python as a scanned ecosystem
Both frontend/package.json and backend/requirements.txt (or their packages) appear in the report
The report includes a summary table or section listing finding counts by severity across all ecosystems

evals.description: Clean project with only a Cargo.toml whose dependencies have no known vulnerabilities. The report must say 'no vulnerabilities found' clearly rather than showing an empty table with no explanation.
evals.setup:
mkdir -p /tmp/eval-depaudit-3/src && cd /tmp/eval-depaudit-3 && git init && cat > Cargo.toml << 'EOF'
[package]
name = "clean-app"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

[dependencies]
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
EOF
cat > src/main.rs << 'EOF'
fn main() {}
EOF
evals.expected_output: Report identifies the Rust ecosystem, states that cargo audit (or fallback) was run, and clearly states that no vulnerabilities were found. The report does not falsely claim findings.

assertions.text: The report identifies Rust as a scanned ecosystem
The report explicitly states that no vulnerabilities were found (not just an empty section)
The report states whether cargo audit was used or a fallback was applied

evals.description: Node.js project where no audit tool reports vulnerabilities but npm outdated shows several packages with newer versions available. The outdated section of the report must be populated even when the vulnerabilities section is empty.
evals.expected_output: Report runs npm outdated and lists express and/or chalk as having newer versions available. The vulnerabilities section is either empty or minimal. The outdated section is not omitted just because no CVEs were found.

assertions.text: The report includes an outdated packages section (not just vulnerabilities)
At least one package is listed as having a newer version available
The report shows both the currently installed version and the available latest version for outdated packages
package.json and lock files are not modified
